role.altitude: The inspector keeps judging parts, handling rejects, talking with the line and recommending fixes; copying gauge readings, filling paper tags and typing report tables shrink.
skills_to_grow: Coding defects consistently so SPC and Pareto views can be trusted
role.ambitious_version: An inspector who spots a drifting process from the control chart before it makes scrap.

tasks.short: Decide that parts fail the specification, record the rejection with a defect code, get disposition for costly lots, discard or reject the products, and have the scrap booked.

steps.what: Inspector compares measured values with the specification limits
Inspector decides whether products or materials fail the specification from measurements and visual checks
Inspector writes the rejection on a paper reject tag and the reject list: order, part, quantity and defect
Quality engineer decides scrap, rework or concession for rejected lots above the value limit
Inspector discards or rejects the products: moves them to the scrap, rework or quarantine area
Production clerk types the reject list into the ERP as scrap or rework
Production clerk checks the final scrap and rework postings against the reject records: order, part, quantity, defect code, and whether each disposition matches the quality engineer's decision
Production clerk releases the approved scrap and rework postings to the ERP

approvals.approved_version: The day's scrap and rework postings with order, part, quantity, defect code and disposition exactly as checked by the production clerk in s7, posted once to the ERP scrap and rework transactions; any change needs a new check.

tasks.design: Measured characteristics from connected gauges flow into the SPC software, which flags values outside the limits; visual defects are still judged by the inspector. The inspector records each rejection on a tablet form in the {OPS_SYSTEM} (MES): scan the job traveller, tap the defect code and count the actual rejected quantity. Lots above the value limit go to the quality engineer for disposition, and the form prepares the scrap or rework postings for the {ERP}, so the clerk no longer types the paper list. The clerk checks the day's postings against the reject records and the engineer's dispositions and releases them; recording a rejection on the form is an ordinary save and needs no approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rejections lived on paper tags and lists that were typed into the ERP days later.
tasks.enabler_now: MES tablet forms post scrap transactions to the ERP; SPC software reads gauges directly.
tasks.still_hard: Visual defects and borderline parts need the inspector's eye.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing when a borderline part will fail at the customer.
tasks.altitude: Less writing; reject decisions stay with the inspector and disposition with the quality engineer.

reach.task: Book scrap and rework in the ERP
reach.learn: Whether scrap is booked the same day once the form posts it.

evidence.claim: SPC software reads gauges, CMMs and PLCs, raises alarms and links to the ERP quality module.
Per-operator records in the MES can monitor staff performance and need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the fail decision to scrap booked; root-cause work is a separate task.
Input contract for s1: measured values from gauges connected to the SPC software on about 60% of characteristics; the rest are read by the inspector.

Input contract for s3: order and part from the job traveller barcode printed by production planning; defect code and actual rejected quantity tapped and counted by the inspector in this step; fallback is the paper tag.

Input contract for s6: the reject records from s3 and, above the value limit, the quality engineer's disposition from s4; the MES prepares the postings, the clerk checks them in s7 and releases them to the ERP in s8.
Moving parts and disposition keep their full time; clerk and engineer time are outside the inspector's savings.
unknowns: Rejects per shift and the value limit for disposition.
research_questions: How often do booked scrap quantities differ from what is in the bin?

already_counted.description: Inspector picks the right defect code when a defect does not fit the list.

incremental.description: Inspector suggests changes to the defect code list.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: gauges are connected for only a third of the characteristics and many travellers lack a barcode, so more values are compared and rejects written by hand (10.0); high: about 60% of characteristics connected as assumed (20.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Notice repeated defects or drifting results, notify supervisors or other personnel of production problems, log the problem, request maintenance and follow up.

steps.what: Inspector notices repeated defects or drifting measurements on the check sheet
Inspector notifies the supervisor or operators of the production problem at the line or by phone
Inspector writes the problem: in the paper shift log today, on the tablet issue form after the change
Inspector requests maintenance by phone or paper slip when equipment causes the problem
Inspector checks the final maintenance request: machine, fault, urgency and the maintenance queue it goes to
Inspector releases the approved maintenance request to the maintenance queue
Inspector follows up whether the problem is fixed

approvals.approved_version: The maintenance request with machine, fault and urgency exactly as checked by the inspector in s5, released once to the named maintenance queue; any change needs a new check.

tasks.design: For characteristics measured on connected gauges, the SPC software applies control chart rules and alarms on drift, so the inspector does not plot trends by hand. Problems are logged on a tablet issue form in the {OPS_SYSTEM} (MES) instead of the paper shift log, and an equipment problem on that form becomes a draft maintenance request; the inspector checks machine, fault, urgency and queue, then releases it to the maintenance queue. Logging the problem on the form is an ordinary save and needs no approval. Telling the supervisor at the line and following up stay with the inspector.
tasks.previous_blocker: Trends were seen only by someone reading paper check sheets, and requests went by phone.
tasks.enabler_now: SPC alarms and MES issue forms that route to maintenance are standard configuration.
tasks.still_hard: Problems seen by eye, such as a change in surface finish.
tasks.human_edge: Getting the line to stop before scrap piles up.
tasks.altitude: Less writing and phoning; decision rights do not change.

reach.learn: Whether requests from the issue form carry enough detail to act on.

evidence.claim: SPC software applies control chart rules and raises alarms from gauge readings.
Issue logs naming operators can monitor performance and need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from spotting a problem to following it up; the repair is outside.
Input contract for s1: readings from gauges connected to the SPC software, about 60% of characteristics; the rest come from the inspector's check sheet.
Input contract for s4: the issue record the inspector creates in s3, with machine and problem type; the MES prepares the maintenance request, which the inspector checks in s5 and releases in s6.

Talks at the line, writing the problem and follow-up keep their full time; the problem record is a first write. s1 keeps 70 because drift alarms replace plotting by hand for connected characteristics; s4 keeps 40 because the request is prepared from the issue record.
research_questions: Do SPC alarms catch drift earlier than the inspector did?

already_counted.description: Inspector checks SPC alarms that turn out to be measurement errors.

incremental.description: Inspector keeps problem types on the issue form current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: most problems are seen by eye, such as surface finish, so few alarms help and requests are still written (5.6); high: about 60% of characteristics on connected gauges as assumed (11.8).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collect measurement results, fill the report tables, write test or inspection reports with findings, recommendations and needed repairs, attach photos, have the report signed and send it.

steps.what: Inspector collects results from gauges, CMM printouts and check sheets
Inspector types the results into the report template
Inspector edits the drafted findings describing test or inspection results

loop.input: The out-of-specification results with their limits and the defect codes from the inspection record.
loop.output: Draft finding sentences per failed characteristic; recommendations and needed repairs are written by the inspector.
loop.check: Every number and limit must match the inspection record, and the inspector confirms that each sentence names the right characteristic, defect and consequence for the part; a sentence that fails either check is rewritten by the inspector.
loop.why_not_simpler: Tables show the values; the customer reads a short description of each finding.

steps.what: Inspector writes the recommendations or needed repairs and completes the inspection report
Inspector adds photos of defects to the report
Quality engineer reviews the final report and signs it
Inspector checks before sending that the report is the version the quality engineer signed and that the customer or supplier named on the order is the recipient
Inspector sends the signed report to the customer or supplier: by e-mail today, by one send from the document system after the change

approvals.approved_version: The inspection report exactly as signed by the quality engineer in s6 and checked by the inspector in s6b, sent once to the customer or supplier named on the order; any change voids the signature and needs a new check.

tasks.design: The CMM program exports its results and connected gauges send readings into the inspection record in the SPC software, and the inspector types only the hand measurements. A report generator fills the tables from that record, and a bounded step drafts finding sentences for failed characteristics, checked against the record; the inspector writes recommendations and repairs. After the quality engineer signs, the inspector checks the version and the recipient and sends exactly the signed report once from the document system.
tasks.previous_blocker: Results were copied from printouts and sheets into a spreadsheet report by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: CMM software and gauge interfaces export results; report generators fill tables from records.
tasks.still_hard: Explaining what a deviation means for the part's use.
tasks.human_edge: Recommending the repair that actually fixes the part.
tasks.altitude: The inspector checks reports instead of typing them; decision rights do not change.

reach.learn: Whether generated reports reduce customer questions on values.

evidence.claim: SPC software reads gauges and CMMs into one record.
Language models can draft short finding sentences whose numbers can be checked against a record.

assumptions: Boundary: from collecting results to the report sent; corrective action is a separate task.

Input contract for s1: CMM program results exported by the CMM software and readings from connected gauges, about 70% of measured values; hand-gauge values typed by the inspector; s1 is priced at that coverage.
Input contract for s2: the inspection record from s1; tables are generated from it, including the typed values.
About half of reports go to customers or suppliers; internal reports are filed instead of sent.
The quality engineer's review is outside the inspector's savings.
Adding photos of defects keeps its full time; nothing in the design changes it.
unknowns: Which gauges and CMMs can export results.
research_questions: How many report errors reach customers before and after?

already_counted.description: Inspector checks generated tables for parts measured partly by hand.

incremental.description: Inspector keeps report templates and CMM export mappings current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: most parts are measured with hand gauges, so results are still collected and typed for most reports (32.2); high: about 70% of values exported from the CMM and gauges as assumed (48.9).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review inspection results and defect history, discuss causes with the line, recommend necessary corrective actions, have them decided and check their effect.

steps.what: Inspector reviews inspection results and defect history in spreadsheets
Inspector discusses likely causes with operators and the supervisor at the line
Inspector decides which corrective action to recommend
Inspector writes the recommended corrective action: on the paper form today; on the quality system form with defect data filled in after the change
Quality engineer decides on the corrective action and assigns it
Inspector checks the effect of the action with follow-up measurements

tasks.design: A defect view in the SPC software shows Pareto charts of defects by code, machine and shift from the inspectors' reject records and the connected gauge readings, and a before-and-after chart for each corrective action. The corrective action form in the quality system has fixed fields linked to that data. Talking with the line, recommending the action and the engineer's decision stay with people.
tasks.previous_blocker: Defect history sat in paper lists and spreadsheets that had to be tallied first.
tasks.enabler_now: SPC software produces Pareto and trend views from coded defects and readings.
tasks.still_hard: Finding the real cause, which the data only points to.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing from an operator what changed on the machine.
tasks.altitude: More time at the line, less tallying; decision rights do not change.

reach.learn: Whether a shared defect view speeds up agreement on causes.

evidence.claim: SPC software computes defect statistics and control charts from gauge data and links to the ERP quality module.
Defect data per machine and shift can point to operators; using it to judge them needs works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from defect history to the effect checked; carrying out the action is outside.

Input contract for s1 and s6: reject records with defect codes produced by inspectors on the MES tablet form when they reject parts, and readings from connected gauges (about 60% of characteristics); fallback is tallying paper lists.

Talks at the line and the engineer's decision keep their full time. s1 keeps 50 because tallying goes and reading the Pareto view stays; s4 keeps 75 because only the defect data fill in and the recommendation is still written; s6 keeps 60 for reading the before-and-after chart.
unknowns: How consistently defects are coded today.
research_questions: Do corrective actions hold longer when checked on a before-and-after chart?

already_counted.description: Inspector checks that defect codes behind a Pareto bar are consistent before recommending.

incremental.description: Inspector keeps defect view filters current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few defect codes and a short history, so the view shows little and most tallying and follow-up stay manual (10.8); high: many machines and shifts with coded defects (20.6).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

job.title: Inspectors, Testers, Sorters, Samplers, and Weighers
